title: How Panchakarma Is Done
metaDescription: A fixture page that names the group's own entities in educational prose.
answerCapsule: Panchakarma is a set of five classical procedures carried out under physician supervision over a period of one to three weeks, with preparation and aftercare phases that are considered part of the procedure rather than optional extras added to it afterwards.

sections.capsule: Panchakarma is carried out at KTAHV, the group's own NABH-accredited hospital, where physicians supervise every stage of the procedure from preparation through to aftercare, and the formulations used are manufactured at the group's own pharmacy nearby in Kerala.
sections.body: The formulations used are made by KAPPL at its WHO-GMP-certified pharmacy. Treatment happens at The Ayurvedic Healing Village under NABH-accredited supervision, and Kairali Ayurvedic Products supplies the oils.

citations.text: National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health (NCCIH). Panchakarma.
